predictedBugs: Next.js App Router rejects arbitrary exports from route modules; the testable drain handler was moved into handler.ts and the production build now accepts the route.
A claimed regular job with no configured adapter could try to transition directly from leased to failed; the worker now records attempt.started first and safely skips a lease lost before execution.
A normal provider success could persist only provider.accepted; the database transition now atomically adds the deterministic provider.final receipt and pgTAP asserts the exact sequence.

A browser disconnect could previously imply completion without provider evidence; the durable revocation queue now records revocation.requested, requires a fenced provider-confirmed transition, and cryptoshreds only after confirmation.
edgeCases: Duplicate cron delivery is bounded by database leases, fencing tokens and workspace-scoped idempotency.
An ambiguous provider outcome enters reconciliation and is never blindly re-executed.
Missing service-role, cron secret, KEK, provider adapter, connector approval or live end-user credentials fails closed without sample fallback.
Unknown or terminal provider revocation never destroys recovery material and remains explicitly disconnected-unconfirmed.

limitations: CodeRabbit is unavailable because the configured WSL environment has no bash; no automated review PASS is claimed.
Google, Mailchimp, Twilio and Meta business operations remain provider-disabled until their Stories 4.1-4.4 and external credentials, approvals and real-account UAT are complete.
No hosted Supabase, Vercel cron, production KEK, provider sandbox or real-account UAT was executed in this story.
